chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Alawi from Sahl ibn Jumhur from Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abdillah al-Alawi from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-'Uranī from 'Amr ibn Jumay' who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about prayer in the painted mosques, and he said, 'I dislike that, but it will not harm you today; and when justice is established, you will see how he acts regarding that.'

key_terms.أَكْرَهُ: I dislike (expressing mild disapproval or recommendation against)
key_terms.الْعَدْلُ: the Justice (referring to the Mahdi or the establishment of divine justice)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying in mosques with images according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the current era of *ghaybah* (occultation), where the presence of images does not invalidate prayer, and the era of the Just Ruler (al-Mahdi), when full implementation of divine law will likely necessitate stricter removal or treatment of images. This hadith highlights the Shia concept of *tadrij* (gradualism) in legal rulings, acknowledging that societal readiness and political authority influence the strictness of religious obligations. It underscores the practical flexibility (*rukhsah*) granted to the community during the interim period while preserving the ideal standard for the final establishment of justice.
